clue.text: West gets back to Welsh town

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress, gives her first name

indicators.note: back tells us the word gets is read from right to left

explanation.surface: Someone called West makes the trip back to a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Mae West was a 1930s Hollywood star, so 'West' gives her first name, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Maesteg is a former mining town in the Llynfi valley of south Wales.

clue.text: Queen's joke in springtime

definitions.note: read as 'Queen is': the title is the form of address for a reigning queen

indicators.note: in puts the word for a joke inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: The Queen tells a joke when spring comes round.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Queen' with its 's read as 'is', as in 'Her Majesty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Her or Your Majesty is the formal title used for a reigning monarch such as a queen.

clue.text: Old bull's punishment

parts.note: ex- means former, old
a papal bull is a formal communication from the Pope

explanation.surface: An old bull is being punished.
explanation.walkthrough: The bull is not an animal but a papal document, and a papal bull was how a Pope cut someone off from the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cut off from the sacraments of the Church is an ecclesiastical penalty.

clue.text: Lay into old wet characters, preferably isosceles

indicators.note: into says the laid item goes inside the other letters
characters suggests the letters of old wet treated as loose symbols to be rearranged

parts.note: what a hen lays is an egg

explanation.surface: Someone lays something into an old wet person, ideally in an even-sided fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges OLD WET into TWOLED, and 'into' places the egg inside. An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, playfully called legs.
explanation.definitionFit: The two equal sides of an isosceles triangle are known as its legs, so such a triangle is jokingly bipedal.

clue.text: Holy object on German lines

parts.note: railway lines are rails

explanation.surface: A sacred relic is carried on German railways.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is the legendary cup of the Last Supper, a sacred object of quest.

clue.text: Iron good when applied to the bone

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
moral means good, virtuous

explanation.surface: An iron tonic is good for your bones.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the femur, the thigh bone.

clue.text: Best one can do as student carried by bird to Kansas

indicators.note: carried by means the student is held inside the bird

parts.note: the fulmar is a grey and white seabird
L is a learner or student, as on L-plates
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: A learner is flown by a bird to Kansas, which is quite an achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: The partner clue to 6 Down; 'student' as L comes from the learner plates on British cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect score in a test is the best result anyone can achieve.

clue.text: Worst one can do, say, at Polo?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken and heard as another word

parts.note: the worst score is zero marks, or marks O

explanation.surface: Doing your worst at polo, the horseback game.
explanation.walkthrough: The partner of 5 Down: the worst score is nought, 'marks O', which sounds like the explorer's first name. 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco is the first name of Polo, the Venetian traveller to China.

clue.text: Yorkshire hooligans scuttle, ignoring all susceptibilities

parts.note: Yorkshire was divided into three Ridings, its historic administrative areas
roughs are rowdy hooligans
a coal scuttle, or hod, is a bucket for carrying coal

explanation.surface: Yorkshire hooligans scurry off with no thought for anyone's feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuttle' looks like a verb but is the coal bucket, a HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride roughshod is an idiom for acting with no regard for others' feelings.

clue.text: Purificatory number for many in Australia

parts.note: L, the Roman numeral for fifty, is a number standing for many

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the word Australia

explanation.surface: A cleansing number for many people in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' picks USTRAL out of AUSTRALIA, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustral water is used in rites of purification, so the word means cleansing.

clue.text: I can do anything with joint account — flatten autumn winds?

definitions.text: I can do anything with joint account — flatten autumn winds?

parts.words: I can do anything with joint account — flatten autumn winds?
parts.note: a handyman who can turn a hand to any job; also, with one F shared, taking the jack off (lowering a car) plus fall (autumn) and trades (trade winds)

explanation.surface: A versatile person with a shared bank account who could even calm the autumn gales.
explanation.walkthrough: Lowering a car means taking the jack off, so 'flatten' is JACK OFF, 'autumn' FALL and 'winds' TRADES; 'joint account' means the F is shared between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who can turn their hand to any job is a proverbial master of none.

clue.text: Wine waiter's river

parts.note: the French term for a wine waiter is jokingly split so that its front part becomes a French river and its tail -lier

explanation.walkthrough: The wine waiter's French title starts with this river's name, as if he were the river's '-lier'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Somme is the river of northern France famous for the First World War battle.

clue.text: Hit on river, one right for satirist

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A satirist is hit on a river by someone righteous.
explanation.definitionFit: A satirist is one who writes lampoons, mocking pieces ridiculing people.

clue.text: Turning grey? Not us — nor him

definitions.text: Turning grey? Not us — nor him

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: We are not going grey, and neither is he.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' rearranges GREY and NOT US; the whole clue describes the answer, who is too young to go grey, so 'nor him' completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person is not yet going grey, which the clue says of him.

clue.text: Boy has note to tinker in boring style

parts.note: Ted is a boy's name
an IOU is a note promising payment
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in the opening of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: A boy has a message for a travelling tinker, delivered dully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'to' are link words; the tinker is Shakespeare's Sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a dull, wearisome way is doing it in a boring manner.

clue.text: Alloy of deuterium found by Russian river

parts.note: D is the chemical symbol for deuterium, heavy hydrogen
the Ural flows from Russia through Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: An alloy containing heavy hydrogen is discovered beside a Russian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Dural, short for duralumin, is a strong light alloy of aluminium and copper.

clue.text: False gold measure for gold in Welsh town

indicators.note: false indicates the letters of gold are given in a counterfeit order

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Fake gold is measured out for real gold in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' turns GOLD into DOLG; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolgellau is a market town in Gwynedd, north Wales.

clue.text: Put up figure

definitions.meaning: a person's body shape or physique

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to construct; the noun means bodily physique or frame.

clue.text: Unqualified success for crusader

parts.note: a bald statement is plain, unqualified
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A crusader enjoys an unqualified triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Baldwin of Boulogne led the First Crusade and became the first Latin King of Jerusalem.

clue.text: City type is sick inside? Demythologise

indicators.note: inside puts the words for is and sick within the city type

parts.note: a dude is a city slicker, a dandy from town
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A city slicker feels sick inside and debunks the myths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' is no town here: a city dude is a smart urban dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: To disillude is to free someone from illusion, to strip away a myth.

clue.text: Is the noble lady deaf?

definitions.meaning: a jocular feminine of earl, formed like countess or princess
without ears, so unable to hear

explanation.surface: Asking whether an aristocratic lady has lost her hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EARL-ESS it is a joke title for an earl's female equal; read as EAR-LESS it means having no ears. 'Is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no ears, one cannot hear, so the word is a jocular term for being unable to hear.

clue.text: Attractive object brings plenty to Geordieland

parts.note: loads means plenty
Geordies come from Tyneside, in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A magnetic thing brings lots of goods to Newcastle.
explanation.walkthrough: Geordies are people from Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is naturally magnetic, so it attracts iron.

clue.text: Is perhaps the first lady a riddle?

indicators.note: perhaps suggests is may be given in another order

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: Is the first woman a mystery?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges IS to SI. Riddle here is a coarse sieve, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve for soil or grain.

clue.text: Fish about 10p? Throw out!

indicators.note: about puts the fish around the other letters

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman numeral ten
p is a penny

explanation.surface: Ten pence for a fish? Get out!
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone is to throw them out.

clue.text: Completely lost voice and note from anaesthetic

indicators.note: lost means these letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: altogether means completely
alto is a singing voice
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone completely lost their voice, and a note, from being anaesthetised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' takes ALTO and G from ALTOGETHER; 'from' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was one of the first general anaesthetics used in surgery.

clue.text: United without success? About fifty cups here, you hypocrite!

indicators.note: without means outside, so united goes around success

parts.note: wed means united in marriage
a hit is a success

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: A football club without a win, and fifty trophies around: someone is two-faced!
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges L with the letters of CUPS HERE. The phrase is from Matthew 23, where Jesus calls the Pharisees whited sepulchres.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus used the phrase for hypocrites, outwardly clean but rotten within, like a whitewashed tomb.

clue.text: Holy place for Trevor who directs on English lines

parts.note: Sir Trevor Nunn is a British theatre director
RY is short for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A sacred spot for a theatre director on English railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent of nuns is a religious house, so a holy place.

clue.text: Holy place for older American director

indicators.note: a director arranges things, signalling that the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A sacred site for an elderly film director from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'director' rearranges OLDER with US. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in south-west France is a Catholic pilgrimage site of Marian apparitions.
